type-i.def: Rejecting the null hypothesis when it is true: finding convincing evidence for an effect that is not there. Its probability is the significance level $\alpha$.

type-ii.def: Failing to reject the null hypothesis when the alternative is true: missing an effect that is there. Its probability, $\beta$, depends on the true value of the parameter.

power.def: The probability that a test rejects the null hypothesis when a specific alternative value is true, $1 - \beta$. It increases with the sample size, with $\alpha$, and with the distance between the true value and the null value.
